## Motivation

Alternative splicing generates distinct protein isoforms from the same
gene. These isoforms can differ in their binding domains and therefore
in which partners they interact with — meaning a switch from one isoform
to another can rewire a cell's protein interaction network even when
total gene expression does not change.

IsoNetAnalyzeR makes this rewiring quantifiable. Given a list of
differentially expressed isoforms (up- and down-regulated relative to a
reference condition), it maps each isoform onto a protein interaction
network, expands a neighbourhood around it via a virtual pulldown, and
then compares the topology of the up- and down-condition subnetworks
across all genes simultaneously.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Required packages: `igraph`, `cli`, `ggplot2`, `ggraph`, `ggrepel`,
`patchwork`, `fgsea`, `org.Hs.eg.db`, `AnnotationDbi`.

Optional: `future` + `future.apply` (parallel execution), `readxl`

## The session object

Everything in IsoNetAnalyzeR flows through a single S4 session object of
class `IsoNetAnalyzeR`. It holds the interaction network, all analyses,
quick lookups, and network diagnostics. You create one at the start of
every session:

```{r create-session}
library(IsoNetAnalyzeR)

obj <- IsoNetAnalyzeR("my_experiment")
#> Loaded package-internal network: 45231 vertices, 312847 edges.
```

By default the package's built-in isoform interaction network is loaded
automatically. You can supply your own `igraph` object instead:

```{r custom-network}
obj <- IsoNetAnalyzeR("custom", network = my_igraph)
```

Printing the object gives a compact session summary:

```{r show-session}
obj
#> ── IsoNetAnalyzeR session ─────────────────────────────────────
#> Name       : my_experiment
#> Created    : 2025-03-01 09:14:22
#> Network    : 45231 vertices / 312847 edges  [source: package_internal]
#> Analyses   : 0 stored  [none]
#> Lookups    : 0 stored  [none]
#> Diagnostics: not run
#> ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

### Metadata

Arbitrary key–value metadata can be attached to the session at any time:

```{r metadata}
obj <- set_metadata(obj, "author",    "Jane Doe")
obj <- set_metadata(obj, "condition", "tumour_vs_normal")
obj <- set_metadata(obj, "notes",     "First pilot run")
print_metadata(obj)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Network diagnostics

Before running any analysis it is useful to understand the structure of
the underlying network — degree distribution, connected components,
sticky (non-specific) nodes — so you know what to expect and whether any
nodes should be treated with caution.

```{r diagnostics}
obj <- run_network_diagnostics(obj, sticky_method = "quantile", sticky_cutoff = 0.95)

diag <- get_network_diagnostics(obj)
diag
```

The six-panel diagnostic figure covers degree distributions at isoform
and gene level, component size structure, isoforms per gene, clustering
vs degree, and gene connectivity status:

```{r plot-diagnostics}
plot_network_diagnostics(obj)
```

Key slots available on the `NetworkDiagnostics` object:

| Slot | Contents |
|---------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| `@network_stats` | One-row data frame: 19 global statistics |
| `@isoform_degree_table` | Per-isoform: `isoform_id`, `gene_id`, `degree` |
| `@gene_degree_table` | Per-gene: `gene_id`, `degree` |
| `@component_table` | Per-component: `component_id`, `n_nodes`, `n_edges` |
| `@clustering_table` | Per-isoform: `degree`, `clustering_coefficient` |
| `@isoform_per_gene_table` | Per-gene: isoform counts by connectivity status |
| `@sticky_isoform_table` | High-degree isoforms above threshold |
| `@sticky_gene_table` | High-degree genes above threshold |

Sticky nodes are those in the upper tail of the degree distribution.
Their presence in a pulldown result does not necessarily indicate
biological relevance — they may be promiscuous binders. Check
`diag@sticky_isoform_table` before interpreting seed neighbourhoods.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Input format

The differential pulldown expects a long-format table with three
required columns:

| Column       | Description                                        |
|--------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| `gene_id`    | Gene identifier (e.g. Ensembl gene ID)             |
| `isoform_id` | Transcript ID matching vertex names in the network |
| `direction`  | `"up"` or `"down"` (case-insensitive, trimmed)     |

Extra columns are retained but ignored. You can supply a CSV path, an
Excel path, or a data frame directly:

```{r input-example, eval=FALSE}
# From a CSV
obj <- run_differential_pulldown(obj, "tumour_vs_normal", "de_isoforms.csv", order = 1)

# From a data frame already in R
de_table <- data.frame(
  gene_id    = c("ENSG00000012048", "ENSG00000012048", "ENSG00000139618"),
  isoform_id = c("ENST00000357654", "ENST00000471181", "ENST00000380152"),
  direction  = c("up",             "down",            "up")
)
obj <- run_differential_pulldown(obj, "tumour_vs_normal", de_table, order = 1)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Differential pulldown

`run_differential_pulldown()` is the main analysis function. For each
gene it:

1.  Splits isoforms into up-regulated and down-regulated sets.
2.  Runs a virtual pulldown separately for each set: restricts the full
    network to predicted interaction edges (`interact == 1`), expands
    via BFS up to `order` hops, then filters out nodes whose edges are
    predominantly external to the subnetwork (the `cutoff` parameter).
3.  Computes per-node statistics (degree, clustering, distance from
    seed, interaction confidence) for each direction subgraph.
4.  Assembles a cross-gene summary with 35 columns comparing the two
    subgraphs.

```{r run-pulldown}
obj <- run_differential_pulldown(
  obj,
  label   = "tumour_vs_normal",
  input   = "de_isoforms.csv",
  order   = 1,
  confirm = FALSE   # suppress interactive coverage prompt in scripts
)
```

### Parallel execution

For analyses with many genes, parallelism is opt-in via the `future`
package:

```{r parallel}
library(future)
plan(multisession, workers = 4)

obj <- run_differential_pulldown(
  obj, "tumour_vs_normal", "de_isoforms.csv",
  order    = 1,
  parallel = TRUE
)

plan(sequential)
```

### Virtual pulldown parameters

| Parameter | Default | Effect |
|----------------------------|-----------------------|---------------------|
| `order` | — (required) | BFS hops from the seed isoforms. `order = 1` includes direct interactors only. |
| `cutoff` | `obj@metadata$network_cutoff` | Minimum fraction of a candidate node's edges that must be internal to the subnetwork. Nodes below this threshold are discarded as non-specific. |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Accessing results

### Cross-gene summary

The 35-column cross-gene summary has one row per gene and is the primary
starting point for most downstream questions:

```{r cgs}
cgs <- get_cross_gene_summary(obj, "tumour_vs_normal")
```

Selected column groups:

**Topology (per condition):** `up_nodes`, `up_edges`, `up_density`,
`up_avg_degree`, `up_clustering`, `up_starness` (degree centralization;
0 = uniform, 1 = pure hub-and-spoke), `up_genes` — and the equivalent
`down_*` columns.

**Node-set overlap:** `n_shared_nodes`, `n_up_unique`, `n_down_unique`,
`jaccard` (Jaccard index of node-set overlap between conditions).

**Edge rewiring:** `n_edges_gained` (in up but not down), `n_edges_lost`
(in down but not up), `n_edges_shared`.

**Interaction confidence (seeds only):** `up_seed_mean_pi` (mean edge
confidence across up seeds), `up_seed_pi_entropy` (Shannon entropy of
confidence distribution — high entropy means many edges of similar
moderate confidence; low entropy means a few high-confidence
interactions).

```{r cgs-explore}
# Most rewired genes
cgs$delta_edges <- cgs$up_edges - cgs$down_edges
head(cgs[order(-abs(cgs$delta_edges)), c("gene_id", "up_edges", "down_edges",
                                          "n_edges_gained", "n_edges_lost", "jaccard")])

# Genes with very different network partners (low Jaccard)
low_overlap <- cgs[!is.na(cgs$jaccard) & cgs$jaccard < 0.1, ]

# Genes where the up condition recruits many more cross-gene partners
cgs[!is.na(cgs$up_genes) & cgs$up_genes > cgs$down_genes + 5, "gene_id"]
```

Cross-gene scatter and boxplot plots read directly from this table:

```{r cgs-plots}
plot_cross_gene_overview(obj, "tumour_vs_normal")

plot_cross_gene_scatter(obj, "tumour_vs_normal",
                        x_col = "up_nodes", y_col = "down_nodes",
                        label_n = 8, label = "delta")
```

### Per-gene results

For any individual gene you can retrieve per-isoform statistics for both
conditions as a single long-format data frame:

```{r isoform-stats}
iso <- get_isoform_stats(obj, "tumour_vs_normal", "ENSG00000012048")
# Returns: direction, isoform, is_seed, degree, clustering,
#          distance_from_seed, mean_pi, pi_entropy

# Seed isoforms only (distance_from_seed == 0)
iso[iso$is_seed, ]

# Up-condition isoforms sorted by degree
up <- iso[iso$direction == "up", ]
up[order(-up$degree), ]
```

The full `GeneDiffPulldown` object (containing the igraph subgraphs) is
retrieved with `get_gene_result()`:

```{r gene-result}
gr <- get_gene_result(obj, "tumour_vs_normal", "ENSG00000012048")
gr   # show() summary

plot_network(gr)               # side-by-side up vs down
plot_network(gr, mode = "overlay")  # merged overlay coloured by direction
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Component analysis

The component analysis merges all per-gene subgraphs into a single
cross-gene network and decomposes it into connected components.
Components containing seeds from both the up and down condition are
flagged as **mixed** — these represent potential rewiring events where
the same interaction neighbourhood is recruited in both conditions but
by different isoforms.

```{r component-run}
obj <- run_component_analysis(
  obj,
  analysis  = "tumour_vs_normal",
  label     = "comp_both",
  direction = "both",
  level     = "isoform",
  min_component_nodes = 3   # drop singleton and pair components
)
```

### Component overview

`get_component_overview()` returns Tier-1 (structural) and Tier-2
(topological) statistics joined into one wide table — one row per
component:

```{r comp-overview}
overview <- get_component_overview(obj, "tumour_vs_normal", "comp_both")
```

**Tier-1 structural columns:** `n_nodes`, `n_edges`, `density`,
`avg_degree`, `clustering`, `n_seeds`, `n_neighbours`, `seed_fraction`,
`n_seeds_up`, `n_seeds_down`, `n_genes_up`, `n_genes_down`, `mixed`,
`n_shared_nodes`, `shared_fraction`.

**Tier-2 topological columns:** `diameter` (longest shortest path),
`radius` (minimum eccentricity), `degree_centralization` (0 = uniform
degree distribution, 1 = pure star), `topology_class` (`"hub-spoke"`,
`"chain-like"`, or `"clique-like"`).

```{r comp-filter}
# Rewiring candidates
overview[overview$mixed, c("component_id", "n_nodes", "n_seeds_up",
                            "n_seeds_down", "topology_class")]

# Potential master regulators: hub-spoke topology with shared nodes
hub_spoke <- overview[!is.na(overview$topology_class) &
                        overview$topology_class == "hub-spoke" &
                        overview$n_shared_nodes > 0, ]
hub_spoke[order(-hub_spoke$degree_centralization), ]
```

### Per-component node table

For any component, `get_component()` returns a per-node table with hub
betweenness scores for shared nodes:

```{r comp-node}
nodes <- get_component(obj, "tumour_vs_normal", "comp_both", component_id = 1)
# columns: component_id, node, source_gene, seed_direction, is_seed, degree,
#          betweenness, betweenness_norm, betweenness_rank

# Nodes bridging across gene communities (high betweenness within the component)
nodes[!is.na(nodes$betweenness_norm) & nodes$betweenness_norm > 0.5, ]
```

```{r comp-plot}
# Territory plot: neighbours coloured by nearest seed group
plot_component(obj, "tumour_vs_normal", "comp_both", component_id = 1,
               colour_by = "direction", colour_neighbours = TRUE)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Gene set enrichment

### ORA per component

Over-representation analysis tests whether GO biological process terms
are enriched in the gene set of each component, using the full network
gene universe as background:

```{r ora}
obj <- run_component_ora(
  obj,
  analysis           = "tumour_vs_normal",
  component_analysis = "comp_both",
  label              = "ora_bp",
  go_category        = "GO:BP",
  padj_cutoff        = 0.05
)

# All significant terms
get_ora_table(obj, "tumour_vs_normal", "comp_both", "ora_bp", padj_cutoff = 0.05)

# Top 3 terms per component — quick biological overview
get_ora_table(obj, "tumour_vs_normal", "comp_both", "ora_bp", top_n = 3)

# Detailed results for one component
get_ora_table(obj, "tumour_vs_normal", "comp_both", "ora_bp",
              component_id = 1, padj_cutoff = 0.05)
```

### GSEA on topology deltas

`run_fgsea()` ranks all genes by a topology delta score (e.g. the
difference in node count between up and down subgraphs) and runs fgsea
against GO gene sets. This identifies pathways whose member genes are
systematically gaining or losing network connectivity in one condition.

```{r gsea}
obj <- run_fgsea(
  obj,
  analysis  = "tumour_vs_normal",
  label     = "gsea_nodes",
  rank_by   = "delta_nodes"   # up_nodes - down_nodes
)

# Significant pathways
sig <- get_gsea_table(obj, "tumour_vs_normal", "gsea_nodes", padj_cutoff = 0.05)
sig[order(sig$NES), c("pathway", "NES", "padj", "size")]

# The gene ranking used as GSEA input
ranks <- get_gsea_stats(obj, "tumour_vs_normal", "gsea_nodes")
head(ranks, 10)   # genes with the largest up-condition network expansion
```

Available `rank_by` presets:

| Preset               | Delta computed                    |
|----------------------|-----------------------------------|
| `"delta_nodes"`      | `up_nodes − down_nodes`           |
| `"delta_edges"`      | `up_edges − down_edges`           |
| `"delta_density"`    | `up_density − down_density`       |
| `"delta_clustering"` | `up_clustering − down_clustering` |
| `"delta_starness"`   | `up_starness − down_starness`     |
| `"delta_avg_degree"` | `up_avg_degree − down_avg_degree` |

You can also supply a custom named numeric vector via the `stats`
argument.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Quick lookup

For ad hoc exploration of a single isoform or gene without running a
full differential analysis, use `lookup_virtual_pulldown()`:

```{r lookup}
obj <- lookup_virtual_pulldown(
  obj,
  label = "BRCA1_isoform_1",
  seed  = "ENST00000357654",
  order = 2,
  level = "isoform"
)

# Node statistics
stats <- get_lookup_stats(obj, "BRCA1_isoform_1")
stats[stats$is_seed, ]

# The subgraph itself
g <- get_lookup_subgraph(obj, "BRCA1_isoform_1")
igraph::vcount(g)
igraph::ecount(g)

plot_network(get_lookup(obj, "BRCA1_isoform_1"))
```

Gene-level lookup: supply a gene ID and set `level = "gene"` to seed
from all isoforms of that gene simultaneously:

```{r lookup-gene}
obj <- lookup_virtual_pulldown(
  obj,
  label = "BRCA1_gene",
  seed  = "ENSG00000012048",
  order = 1,
  level = "gene"
)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Session management

All analyses and lookups are stored inside the session object under
user-supplied labels. Use the list functions to inspect what has been
run:

```{r list}
list_analyses(obj)   # character vector of analysis labels
list_lookups(obj)    # character vector of lookup labels

# Retrieve a stored analysis object directly
analysis_obj <- get_analysis(obj, "tumour_vs_normal")
```

Sessions can be saved and reloaded with standard R serialisation:

```{r save}
saveRDS(obj, "isonetanalyzer_session.rds")
obj <- readRDS("isonetanalyzer_session.rds")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Typical analysis checklist

1.  `IsoNetAnalyzeR()` — create session
2.  `run_network_diagnostics()` — understand the network; note sticky
    nodes
3.  `run_differential_pulldown()` — core analysis (sequential or
    parallel)
4.  `get_cross_gene_summary()` — identify high-rewiring genes
5.  `plot_cross_gene_overview()` — visual overview of all topology
    metrics
6.  `get_isoform_stats()` + `plot_network()` — drill into genes of
    interest
7.  `run_component_analysis()` — decompose the cross-gene network
8.  `get_component_overview()` — filter for mixed / hub-spoke components
9.  `plot_component()` — visualise rewiring within each component
10. `run_component_ora()` + `get_ora_table()` — biological
    interpretation per component
11. `run_fgsea()` + `get_gsea_table()` — pathway-level topology shifts
12. `saveRDS()` — save the session
